Best mixer grinders for South Indian kitchens under Rs 6,000 (2026)

Affiliate disclosure: this page has affiliate links to Amazon.in and Flipkart. If you buy through them we may earn a commission, at no extra cost to you. Every pick below comes from our own tests, and the notes say where each one fell short.

QUICK PICKS (prices checked 3 October 2026)

Best overall: Vasanta Wetstone 750, Rs 5,490. Smooth batter with no grit, 68 dB, service in 14 Tamil Nadu towns plus Bengaluru and Kochi. [Amazon.in link] [Flipkart link]
Best budget: Annam Basic 500, Rs 2,799. The cheapest here, with slightly grainy batter and the loudest motor. [Amazon.in link] [Flipkart link]
Best for idli-dosa batter: Thenral Batter Pro 1000, Rs 5,950. The only fluffy batter we got, from a 1.8 L batter jar. [Amazon.in link] [Flipkart link]
Quietest: Mouna Silent 600, Rs 5,799. 62 dB, the lowest of the six. [Amazon.in link] [Flipkart link]
Best compact: Chotu Mix 400, Rs 3,499. Fits a 20 cm shelf, but the batter came out coarse. [Amazon.in link] [Flipkart link]
Best warranty: Surabhi Care 650, Rs 5,299. A 5-year motor warranty and service in 22 Tamil Nadu districts and Kerala. [Amazon.in link] [Flipkart link]

HOW WE CHOSE

Two testers worked through all six grinders in September 2026. The main test was batter, because that is what a South Indian kitchen buys a mixer grinder for. In each grinder's wet jar we ground 1 kg of idli rice and 250 g of urad dal and checked the texture after 20 minutes.

We measured noise at 1 metre with the motor on high, using a phone meter. That is good enough to compare these six with each other, but do not compare our numbers with the one printed on a brand's box. As a rough guide, about 10 dB reads as twice as loud to the ear.

Prices were checked on 3 October 2026 and move often. Service reach and warranty are as recorded in our tester notes; confirm both on the brand's own page before you order. We have not run these grinders for months, so the warranty sections describe what a brand promises, not what we have seen fail.

PICK 1. BEST OVERALL: VASANTA WETSTONE 750 (Rs 5,490)

The one we would buy for a home that grinds batter every week and also needs the masala and chutney jars.

Who it is for: families who want smooth batter, a motor you can talk over, and a service centre they can reach.

What testing showed: 750 W with three jars. The batter came out smooth with no grit after 20 minutes. At 68 dB it was the second quietest of the six, behind only the Mouna. Service is listed in 14 Tamil Nadu towns plus Bengaluru and Kochi.

Why it edges out the Surabhi Care 650 for overall: both gave smooth batter, but the Vasanta has 100 W more and runs 4 dB quieter, for Rs 191 more. It was a close call, and the Surabhi wins on warranty.

Pros: smooth batter, low noise for the power, and service that reaches Bengaluru and Kochi as well as 14 Tamil Nadu towns.
Cons: Rs 5,490 is not cheap. Its warranty length is not in our notes [verify]. If you live outside those 14 towns, Bengaluru and Kochi, check the nearest centre before you buy.
Price: Rs 5,490 on 3 October 2026.
Alternative: the Surabhi Care 650 if a long warranty matters more to you than a quieter motor.
[Amazon.in link] [Flipkart link]

PICK 2. BEST BUDGET: ANNAM BASIC 500 (Rs 2,799)

Rs 2,691 cheaper than our top pick, and you can hear and see in the batter where the money went.

Who it is for: a one- or two-person home in Chennai or Coimbatore that grinds batter now and then and wants the lowest price.

What testing showed: 500 W with two jars. The batter was slightly grainy after 20 minutes, not coarse but not smooth either. At 78 dB it was the loudest of the six, 16 dB above the Mouna. Service is in Chennai and Coimbatore only.

Pros: the lowest price in the test, and it still gets through an idli batter.
Cons: grainy batter, the loudest motor here, and only two cities with service. A fault anywhere else means you are arranging a courier yourself. Warranty length is not in our notes [verify].
Price: Rs 2,799 on 3 October 2026.
Alternative: if you can stretch to Rs 5,299, the Surabhi Care 650 gives you smooth batter and a 5-year motor warranty.
[Amazon.in link] [Flipkart link]

PICK 3. BEST FOR IDLI-DOSA BATTER: THENRAL BATTER PRO 1000 (Rs 5,950)

If batter is the main job, this is the one that did it best.

Who it is for: bigger families, or anyone who grinds the week's batter in one go.

What testing showed: 1000 W with three jars, one of them a 1.8 L batter jar. It was the only grinder that gave us fluffy batter after 20 minutes; the rest ranged from smooth down to coarse. At 74 dB it is 6 dB louder than the Vasanta.

Pros: the best batter in the test, and a dedicated batter jar in the box.
Cons: heavy at 4.1 kg, so it will not live comfortably on a high shelf. Louder than most. At Rs 5,950 it sits only Rs 50 under the Rs 6,000 ceiling for this list. Warranty and service reach are not in our notes [verify].
Price: Rs 5,950 on 3 October 2026.
Alternative: the Vasanta Wetstone 750 gives smooth, grit-free batter for Rs 460 less and runs 6 dB quieter.
[Amazon.in link] [Flipkart link]

PICK 4. QUIETEST: MOUNA SILENT 600 (Rs 5,799)

At 62 dB it is the quietest of the six by a clear margin.

Who it is for: flats with thin walls, joint families with early risers, anyone who has stopped grinding in the evening because of the noise.

What testing showed: 600 W with three jars. 62 dB at 1 metre on high was the lowest we measured, 6 dB under the Vasanta and 16 dB under the Annam. The batter came out slightly coarse after 20 minutes.

Pros: by far the quietest motor in the test, and it still comes with three jars.
Cons: slightly coarse batter, and it costs Rs 309 more than the Vasanta, which gave smooth batter at 68 dB. The warranty is 1 year, against five on the Surabhi. Service reach is not in our notes [verify].
Price: Rs 5,799 on 3 October 2026.
Alternative: the Vasanta Wetstone 750 if you can live with 6 dB more noise for better batter.
[Amazon.in link] [Flipkart link]

PICK 5. BEST COMPACT: CHOTU MIX 400 (Rs 3,499)

It fits a 20 cm shelf, and that is the whole case for it.

Who it is for: small kitchens, hostel rooms, couples who make chutney and the odd dosa batter and have no counter to spare.

What testing showed: 400 W with two jars. The batter was coarse after 20 minutes, the weakest texture of the six. At 70 dB it sat in the middle of the pack for noise.

Pros: the footprint, and a price Rs 1,991 under the Vasanta.
Cons: coarse batter, the lowest wattage in the test, only two jars. Warranty and service reach are not in our notes [verify].
Price: Rs 3,499 on 3 October 2026.
Alternative: the Annam Basic 500 is Rs 700 cheaper and gave slightly grainy batter instead of coarse, if your shelf can take a bigger body.
[Amazon.in link] [Flipkart link]

PICK 6. BEST WARRANTY: SURABHI CARE 650 (Rs 5,299)

Smooth batter, a 5-year motor warranty, and the cheapest of the four models above Rs 5,000.

Who it is for: households in Tamil Nadu districts and in Kerala, where a nearby service centre matters more than the last few decibels.

What testing showed: 650 W with three jars. The batter was smooth after 20 minutes. Noise was 72 dB, 4 dB louder than the Vasanta. The motor carries a 5-year warranty, and service is listed in 22 Tamil Nadu districts and Kerala.

Pros: smooth batter, the longest warranty in the group, Rs 191 cheaper than the Vasanta and Rs 500 cheaper than the Mouna.
Cons: noisier than the Vasanta and the Mouna. The five years cover the motor; ask what the warranty says about jars and blades before you pay [verify].
Price: Rs 5,299 on 3 October 2026.
Alternative: the Vasanta Wetstone 750 for a little more power and a little less noise.
[Amazon.in link] [Flipkart link]

COMPARISON TABLE

Model | Price (3 Oct 2026) | Watts | Jars | Batter after 20 min | Noise at 1 m | Warranty and service
Vasanta Wetstone 750 | Rs 5,490 | 750 | 3 | Smooth, no grit | 68 dB | Service in 14 TN towns, Bengaluru, Kochi; warranty [verify]
Annam Basic 500 | Rs 2,799 | 500 | 2 | Slightly grainy | 78 dB | Service in Chennai, Coimbatore; warranty [verify]
Thenral Batter Pro 1000 | Rs 5,950 | 1000 | 3 (1.8 L batter jar) | Fluffy | 74 dB | [verify]
Mouna Silent 600 | Rs 5,799 | 600 | 3 | Slightly coarse | 62 dB | 1-year warranty; service [verify]
Chotu Mix 400 | Rs 3,499 | 400 | 2 | Coarse | 70 dB | [verify]
Surabhi Care 650 | Rs 5,299 | 650 | 3 | Smooth | 72 dB | 5-year motor warranty; service in 22 TN districts, Kerala

BUYING GUIDE

Start with batter, not wattage. In our test the three machines at 400 to 600 W never did better than slightly grainy batter, and the 650 W and 750 W models both gave smooth batter. But power is not the whole story: the 600 W Mouna came out coarser than the 650 W Surabhi, so look at the batter result and not only the number on the box.

Check what the wattage means. Some boxes print a peak figure, not the rated one. Look for the rated wattage in the specification sheet, and for overload protection if the grinder will run for 20 minutes at a stretch [verify on each box].

Look at where the repair happens. A mixer grinder is a machine you will send for service at some point. Find the nearest centre to your pin code before you order, and ask whether the warranty covers the jars and blades, not just the motor.

Count the jars you will use. Two jars are enough for batter and chutney. A third jar is for dry masala. A dedicated batter jar, like the 1.8 L one on the Thenral, helps only if you grind large batches.

Think about the shelf and the sleepers. A 4.1 kg grinder is a different daily habit from one that fits a 20 cm shelf, and a 62 dB motor is a different morning from a 78 dB one.

FAQ

Do I need 750 W for idli batter?
No. A 650 W grinder gave us smooth batter, as did the 750 W. At 600 W and below, none of our batters got past slightly grainy.

Which one is the quietest?
The Mouna Silent 600 at 62 dB, measured at 1 metre on high with a phone meter.

Which is best if I live outside Chennai?
Service in our notes: the Vasanta in 14 Tamil Nadu towns plus Bengaluru and Kochi, the Surabhi in 22 Tamil Nadu districts and Kerala. The Annam has service in Chennai and Coimbatore only.

Is the Rs 2,799 Annam a false economy?
For occasional use, no. For weekly batter, probably: it was grainy and the loudest, and its service reach is the narrowest we have on record.

Why is your top pick not the one with the longest warranty?
Because the Vasanta gave the same smooth batter as the Surabhi, with more power and less noise, for Rs 191 more. If warranty ranks first for you, pick the Surabhi.

Circle Sunday 1 November in your calendar. Two of this week's fee changes land that day, and a third, on WhatsApp messages, is already in your October bill. Pehle margin, phir marketing.

LEAD: THE BEAUTY FEE JUMPS TWO POINTS
Marketplace X is raising its referral fee on beauty and personal care from 8% to 10%, for orders above Rs 500, from 1 November 2026. Sellers got the notice on Monday 5 October.

Two points sounds small. It is charged on every qualifying order, and it comes straight out of your margin. On a Rs 600 product, the fee goes up by Rs 12 per order. Ship 1,000 of those a month and that is Rs 12,000 gone, every month, with no change in what the customer pays.

Two things to do before 1 November. First, read the notice and confirm whether the 10% applies to the whole order value or only the part above Rs 500 [verify in the notice]. samples.text:
GST NOTICES FOR D2C FOUNDERS
6 common notice types and how to respond to each

[Copy-deck note for design: boxes marked CALLOUT, tables marked TABLE, and the one-page checklist marked PRINT PAGE. Every [bracket] is a fact the firm must fill or confirm before the designer sees the file.]

INTRODUCTION: WHAT TO DO WHEN THE NOTICE LANDS

You open your email on a Monday and find a PDF from the GST portal. The subject line says "Notice". There is a reference number, a section you have never heard of, and a date. Your accountant is travelling. Your first thought is not "what does the law say". It is "how bad is this, and how long do I have".

This guide answers those two questions for the six notices D2C founders get most often. It is written for founders and finance heads of D2C brands with Rs 5-50 crore of revenue, selling on their own site and on marketplaces. At that size you file monthly returns, you are probably under e-invoicing and annual reconciliation [verify current turnover thresholds], and the department holds more data about your sales than you may expect. Your marketplaces report their side of every order.

It is not for you if you have received a summons, a search notice or anything from the DGGI or the police. Those need a lawyer on the first day, not a guide.

By the end you will be able to do three things. Read the form number on any notice and know which stage you are at. Find your reply deadline. Start the first three actions the same day, without waiting for anyone.

Each chapter has the same shape: what the notice is, why D2C brands get it, what to check first, how to respond, the mistake to avoid, and a tool you can copy. Every chapter ends with a place for a real case from our files. Our credentials: [proof: number of D2C notice replies this firm has filed, and for how many brands].

CALLOUT: three rules for every notice
1. Read the form number and the due date before anything else. The form number tells you the stage.
2. Never ignore it, and never pay it just to make it go away. Payment is a decision, not a reply.
3. Reply on the portal, in the form the notice names, with documents attached. A phone call or a loose email to an officer is not a reply.

CALLOUT: read any notice in five minutes
Look for six things in this order: who issued it (the officer's name, designation and jurisdiction), the form number, the section, the period it covers, the amount it names, and the date by which you must reply. Write them on one line at the top of a blank page. If any of the six is missing or unclear, that is your first question to the officer.

CHAPTER 1. THE SCRUTINY NOTICE (FORM ASMT-10)

What it is. An officer compared your returns with other data and found differences. Under Section 61 and Rule 99 of the CGST Rules, the officer sends you the differences in Form ASMT-10 and asks for your explanation. It is a request for an answer, not yet a demand for tax.

Your deadline. 30 days from the date the notice is served, or a longer period if the officer allows it. Ask for more time in writing on the portal if you need it. Do not assume you have it.

Why D2C brands get it. Three causes come up again and again. First, the sales you reported in GSTR-1 do not match what a marketplace reported for you. Marketplaces collect tax at source under Section 52 and report your supplies in their own return, GSTR-8. [verify the TCS rate currently in force.] Second, the input tax credit you claimed in GSTR-3B is higher than GSTR-2B shows. Third, cancelled orders and returns: a credit note was issued late, in the wrong month, or not at all.

What to check first. Open the annexure to the notice. Note which months and which figures it names. Pull the same months from three places: your GSTR-1, your GSTR-3B and the marketplace's settlement or GSTR-8 data. Do this before you write a word.

How to respond. You have two options. Option A: accept the difference, pay the tax with interest through Form DRC-03, and tell the officer in Form ASMT-11. Option B: explain, in ASMT-11, with a reconciliation and documents. If the officer is satisfied, you receive Form ASMT-12 and the matter closes. If not, the officer may go to an audit, a special audit, an inspection, or a demand under Section 73 or 74. Your first reply is your best chance to stop that.

The mistake to avoid. A one-line reply saying "difference is due to timing". An officer cannot accept a reason without a table and documents behind it.

TABLE: reconciliation sheet for an ASMT-10 reply
Month | Figure in your returns | Figure in the other source | Difference | Reason | Document attached
Example row (illustration, not a client case): September | GSTR-1 net taxable value Rs 41,20,000 | Marketplace report Rs 42,05,000 | Rs 85,000 | Orders cancelled and reversed in October | Marketplace cancellation report, October credit notes

At 18%, a Rs 85,000 difference means Rs 15,300 of tax if the reason is not accepted. Know the number before you decide between Option A and Option B.

A monthly habit that prevents this notice: before you file GSTR-3B, sum the marketplace settlement reports for the month, deduct the orders cancelled or returned, and compare the net with your GSTR-1 taxable value. Keep the sheet. If an officer asks in two years, the answer already exists, month by month.

[Client case: D2C [category] brand, ASMT-10, difference Rs [x], outcome [y].]

CHAPTER 2. THE SYSTEM INTIMATION (FORMS DRC-01B AND DRC-01C)

What it is. A message generated by the GST portal, not by an officer. Under Rules 88C and 88D, the portal compares your GSTR-3B with other data. Form DRC-01B flags that the tax you reported in GSTR-1 is higher than the tax you paid in GSTR-3B. Form DRC-01C flags that the credit you claimed in GSTR-3B is higher than the credit the portal shows in GSTR-2B. [verify the form names and effective dates.]

Your deadline. The rules give a short window, seven days [verify the current window]. This is the tightest clock in this guide.

Why D2C brands get it. A D2C brand has high order volume and many small invoices. GSTR-1 is built from orders and invoices, while GSTR-3B is often typed or uploaded at the end of the month by someone else. When they drift apart by a large amount, the portal notices first.

What to check first. The intimation shows the difference. These intimations apply only above notified thresholds on amount and percentage [verify the thresholds], so a small gap will not trigger one.

How to respond. Either pay the difference through Form DRC-03 and report it in the portal, or explain it in the reply section of the form, with the reason and the document. If the reason is a late invoice or a data entry error, say which invoice, which month, and what you have corrected.

If you do neither. The rules say the next steps can include a block on filing your next GSTR-1 and proceedings for recovery or a demand notice [verify Rule 59(6), Rule 88C and Section 79]. A blocked GSTR-1 means a missed marketplace reconciliation next month.

The mistake to avoid. Treating it as a reminder from a system and letting the window pass.

TABLE: three comparisons to run before you file GSTR-3B each month
Compare | Source A | Source B | Action if different
Tax liability | GSTR-1 for the month | GSTR-3B draft | Fix GSTR-3B or amend in the next GSTR-1
Input tax credit | GSTR-2B for the month | GSTR-3B credit table | Claim only what GSTR-2B shows [verify Section 16(2)(aa)]
Marketplace sales | Marketplace monthly statement | GSTR-1 | Find the cancelled, returned or unreported orders

[Client case: D2C [category] brand, DRC-01B, difference Rs [x], outcome [y].]

CHAPTER 3. THE NOTICE FOR NOT FILING A RETURN (FORM GSTR-3A)

What it is. If you do not file a return, the system sends Form GSTR-3A under Section 46 and Rule 68. It asks you to file the missing return.

Your deadline. 15 days from the notice.

Why D2C brands get it. Typical reasons: a nil month, a change of accountant, or a return held back because a marketplace payout is under dispute.

What to check first. List every return that has not been filed: GSTR-1 and GSTR-3B, by month. Check the tax payable for each month before you file; do not file a nil return where there were sales.

How to respond. File the pending returns. Pay the tax, the interest and the late fee. Interest on tax paid late is 18% a year under Section 50. [verify the late fee per day currently in force.] File the oldest month first, so the later months can follow.

If you do nothing. The officer can assess your tax on a best-judgment basis under Section 62 and send an order. If you file a valid return within 30 days of that order, the order is treated as withdrawn, but interest and late fee stay payable. File before the order, not after it.

The mistake to avoid. Waiting for the marketplace dispute to end before filing. The return is due on its date whatever the payout status.

TABLE: missing-returns tracker
Period | GSTR-1 filed? | GSTR-3B filed? | Tax due | Days late | Interest at 18% a year
Example (illustration): April | Yes | No | Rs 1,00,000 | 45 | Rs 2,219 (1,00,000 x 18% x 45 / 365)

[Client case: D2C [category] brand, GSTR-3A, [n] months pending, outcome [y].]

CHAPTER 4. THE SHOW-CAUSE NOTICE FOR CANCELLING YOUR REGISTRATION (FORM REG-17)

What it is. The officer proposes to cancel your GST registration under Section 29 and asks why it should not be cancelled. One ground in the law is that a regular taxpayer has not filed returns for a continuous period of six months. There are others.

Your deadline. 7 working days from service of the notice, to reply in Form REG-18 (Rule 22).

Why D2C brands get it. A brand that stops filing, a registered address that no longer exists, a business that moved from one state to another without amending the registration. For a D2C brand, an active GSTIN is also what marketplaces and payment partners check, so a cancelled one stops the business. [verify how suspension affects marketplace listings and payouts.]

What to check first. The ground named in the notice. If the ground is non-filing, file the returns first, then reply. If it is the address, gather the rent agreement, electricity bill and photographs.

How to respond. Reply in Form REG-18 within the window. Attach proof that the problem is fixed. If the officer drops the proceedings, you receive an order saying so. If registration is cancelled, you can apply for revocation in Form REG-21 within 30 days of the cancellation order.

The mistake to avoid. Planning to "register again" if it is cancelled. Registering again does not wipe out old returns or tax already due.

TABLE: the seven-working-day plan
Day 1: Read the ground, list the facts, check for pending returns.
Day 2: Collect documents (returns, address proof, agreements).
Day 3: File any missing returns, with tax and interest.
Day 4: Draft the REG-18 reply and attachments.
Day 5: Review with your CA, then file. Keep two days in hand.

[Client case: D2C [category] brand, REG-17, ground [x], outcome [y].]

CHAPTER 5. THE NOTICE BEFORE A REFUND IS REJECTED (FORM RFD-08)

What it is. If you claimed a refund and the officer is minded to reject it, wholly or partly, you receive Form RFD-08 with the reasons. Under Rule 92, no refund application can be rejected without giving you a chance to be heard.

Your deadline. 15 days from the notice, to reply in Form RFD-09.

Why D2C brands get it. Brands that export, or whose tax on inputs is higher than on sales, claim refunds of unused input credit. [verify which refund routes apply to your supplies.] Refund claims are the most paperwork-heavy part of GST: the officer matches your invoices with the shipping or export documents.

What to check first. The reasons listed. Common reasons are document gaps: invoices that do not match the shipping bill, missing proof of export payment, or input credit that does not appear in GSTR-2B. A refund application is allowed within two years of the relevant date under Section 54 [verify the relevant date for your type of supply].

How to respond. Reply in RFD-09 with a point-by-point answer, a statement matching each invoice with its shipping bill and payment proof, and a request for a personal hearing. If the officer still rejects, you receive an order and can appeal.

The mistake to avoid. Replying with a covering letter and no matching statement. The officer rejects what they cannot match.

TABLE: refund reply pack
Document | What it proves | Match against
Tax invoice | The sale | Shipping bill and GSTR-1
Shipping bill / export document | The goods left India | Invoice number and value
Payment proof | You were paid | Invoice and bank credit
GSTR-2B and GSTR-3B | Input credit is real | Credit claimed in the refund

[Client case: D2C [category] brand, RFD-08, refund Rs [x], outcome [y].]

CHAPTER 6. THE SHOW-CAUSE NOTICE FOR TAX DEMAND (FORM DRC-01)

What it is. This is the serious one: a formal demand, called a show-cause notice, that you owe tax, interest and penalty. For a financial year up to 2023-24 it is issued under Section 73 (no fraud alleged) or Section 74 (fraud, wilful misstatement or suppression). From 2024-25 Section 74A replaces them [verify]. The time limits differ by section [verify]. Form DRC-01 is the summary of the notice.

Your deadline. The date written on the notice. Reply in Form DRC-06.

Why D2C brands get it. It is where an unanswered ASMT-10, an unexplained mismatch or an input credit dispute ends up.

What to check first. Which section is invoked, which years, what amount, and whether the notice alleges fraud. A fraud allegation changes the penalty a great deal. It also changes how carefully the reply must be written.

How to respond. If you agree with part of it, pay that part through Form DRC-03 within 30 days of the notice; under Section 73, tax and interest paid within 30 days end the proceedings with no penalty [verify; Section 74 requires a penalty of 25% of the tax]. Reply to the rest in Form DRC-06 with a point-by-point answer, a computation, documents and legal grounds. Ask for a personal hearing in writing. A hearing is your chance to speak to the officer, not a formality.

If an order follows. The order comes in Form DRC-07. You can appeal an order, not the notice. File the appeal within three months of the order in Form APL-01, with a pre-deposit of 10% of the tax in dispute, plus the amount you admit [verify the pre-deposit rules and the cap].

The mistake to avoid. Replying late in a hurry, or only with sympathy. A reply that answers each paragraph of the notice, with documents, is read differently from a request for mercy.

TABLE: structure of a DRC-06 reply
1. Cover letter: notice number, date, section.
2. Para-wise reply: one answer per allegation.
3. Computation: your figure against the department's.
4. Documents: indexed and numbered.
5. Legal grounds: limitation, wrong section, double counting.
6. Prayer: drop the demand, or hold a personal hearing.

Illustration, not a client case: a brand is told it short-paid Rs 3,00,000 of tax and pays it 240 days after the due date. Interest at 18% a year is 3,00,000 x 18% x 240 / 365, which is about Rs 35,507. Interest runs for every day the tax stayed unpaid, so a quick, partial payment of the amount you agree with reduces it. Do the same sum for your own notice before you reply.

[Client case: D2C [category] brand, DRC-01, demand Rs [x], outcome [y].]

PRINT PAGE: ONE-PAGE NOTICE TRIAGE

Form | What it means | Reply window | Where you reply
ASMT-10 | Scrutiny: differences in returns | 30 days, extendable | ASMT-11 on the portal
DRC-01B / DRC-01C | System intimation: tax or credit gap | Short, about 7 days [verify] | Reply section, or DRC-03
GSTR-3A | You have not filed a return | 15 days | File the return
REG-17 | Proposed cancellation of registration | 7 working days | REG-18
RFD-08 | Proposed rejection of a refund | 15 days | RFD-09
DRC-01 | Show-cause notice for tax demand | Date on the notice | DRC-06

Ten checks for the day the notice lands:
1. Note the form number, the reference number and the date it was served.
2. Mark the reply date on your calendar, with a date two days earlier.
3. Download the notice and every annexure.
4. Tell your CA the same day.
5. Do not pay anything before you know what the number is for.
6. List the months and figures named in the notice.
7. Pull your GSTR-1, GSTR-3B, GSTR-2B and marketplace statements for those months.
8. Fill in a reconciliation sheet. Find out what is real.
9. Reply in the right form, on the portal, with indexed documents.
10. Keep a copy of the reply and the portal acknowledgement.

NEXT STEP: BOOK A 20-MINUTE GST HEALTH-CHECK CALL

Notices are cheap to answer early and expensive to answer late. Many of them start as a small mismatch that nobody looked at.

In the 20-minute call, we run the three comparisons from Chapter 2 on your last three months of returns: GSTR-1 against GSTR-3B, GSTR-2B against your input credit, and your marketplace statements against your sales. You leave with a one-page list of what could become a notice, and what to fix first.

7 Indian D2C founders on the one change that cut their customer acquisition cost

INTRO
Customer acquisition cost, or CAC, is the number that decides whether a D2C brand has a business or a habit of buying ads. Most advice on cutting it is a list of fifty tactics. We wanted one tactic per founder, with the numbers.

Between 14 and 25 September 2026 we asked seven founders at early-stage D2C brands, in seven cities, the same question: what was the one change that cut your CAC, and what was it before and after? All seven made the change themselves and gave us before and after figures, in categories from skincare to pet food. Every quote below was approved by the person who said it.

The short answer: all seven cut CAC. The smallest cut was 18%, the largest 36%.

Disclosure: two of the seven, Aditi Sharma and Rohan Iyer, are clients of [Agency name]. Their results are included on the same terms as the others.

THE SYNTHESIS
Three patterns run through the answers.

First, the five biggest cuts came from changing what the shopper sees or is offered before they buy. Rohan Iyer's Rs 49 sampling sachet cut CAC by 36%, Aditi Sharma's unboxing videos by 32%, Vikram Rathore's founder-led Lives by 30%, Nisha Deshpande's free gift by 29%, and Karan Malhotra's move to three broad audiences by 27%.

Second, the two smaller cuts came after the click. Sneha Pillai's 5% prepaid discount cut CAC by 20%, after returns. Fatima Khan's WhatsApp cart recovery cut it by 18%.

Third, speed. Five of the seven saw the cut within 10 weeks, and the longest took four months.

Where they disagreed. Karan says creative beats targeting. Fatima says fixing what happens after the click beats any change to the ads. On these seven answers, the numbers lean towards Karan: the largest cuts all happened before the purchase. But Fatima's fix is a separate lever, not a rival one, and you can run both.

Our verdict, with caution. Seven founders is a small sample. The figures are self-reported, the categories differ, and the time windows run from six weeks to four months. Read this as a direction, not a league table. And two of the three biggest cuts came from our own clients, so weigh those two with that in mind.

THE NUMBERS AT A GLANCE
Founder | Change | CAC before | CAC after | Cut | Window
Rohan Iyer | Rs 49 sampling sachet as first order | Rs 640 | Rs 410 | 36% | 2 months
Aditi Sharma | Customer unboxing videos | Rs 820 | Rs 560 | 32% | 3 months
Vikram Rathore | Founder-led Instagram Lives twice a week | Rs 1,050 | Rs 730 | 30% | 4 months
Nisha Deshpande | Free gift instead of 20% off | Rs 760 | Rs 540 | 29% | 6 weeks
Karan Malhotra | Meta ads cut to 3 broad audiences | Rs 710 | Rs 520 | 27% | 8 weeks
Sneha Pillai | 5% prepaid discount (after returns) | Rs 880 | Rs 700 | 20% | 10 weeks
Fatima Khan | WhatsApp cart recovery within 30 minutes | Rs 950 | Rs 780 | 18% | 6 weeks
The percentages are our arithmetic on the founders' figures, rounded to the nearest whole number.

THE ANSWERS, BY THEME

Theme 1. Change what people see before they click

Aditi Sharma, founder, skincare brand, Delhi [brand name, link]
She replaced studio product shots with customers' unboxing videos. CAC went from Rs 820 to Rs 560 in 3 months, a fall of 32%.
[Approved quote, 25-40 words.]
Our takeaway: a real customer opening the box did the job a studio shoot was meant to do. Ask your next ten customers for a 15-second clip.

Karan Malhotra, founder, protein snacks, Pune [brand name, link]
He cut his Meta ads to three broad audiences. CAC went from Rs 710 to Rs 520 in 8 weeks, down 27%.
[Approved quote, 25-40 words.]
Our takeaway: this change removes work instead of adding it. Karan's view is that creative beats targeting.

Vikram Rathore, co-founder, ethnic menswear, Jaipur [brand name, link]
He went live on Instagram twice a week as the founder. CAC went from Rs 1,050 to Rs 730 in 4 months, down 30%.
[Approved quote, 25-40 words.]
Our takeaway: the slowest result here, and the one with the highest starting CAC. A founder on camera needs a schedule you can keep.

Theme 2. Make the first order easier to say yes to

Rohan Iyer, co-founder, coffee, Chennai [brand name, link]
He made a Rs 49 sampling sachet the first order. CAC went from Rs 640 to Rs 410 in 2 months, down 36%, the biggest cut in this roundup. Rohan is a client of [Agency name].
[Approved quote, 25-40 words.]
Our takeaway: a low-risk first purchase lets a customer try the product before committing to a full pack.

Nisha Deshpande, founder, pet food, Nagpur [brand name, link]
She gave a free gift on the first order instead of 20% off. CAC went from Rs 760 to Rs 540 in 6 weeks, down 29%.
[Approved quote, 25-40 words.]
Our takeaway: she traded a 20% discount for a free gift and CAC still fell by 29%, so a discount is not the only way to win a first order.

Theme 3. Fix what happens after the click

Fatima Khan, founder, modest fashion, Hyderabad [brand name, link]
She started WhatsApp cart recovery within 30 minutes of abandonment. CAC went from Rs 950 to Rs 780 in 6 weeks, down 18%.
[Approved quote, 25-40 words.]
Our takeaway: the smallest cut, but it needs no new ad, and the timing is the instruction: 30 minutes, not the next day.

Sneha Pillai, founder, baby care, Kochi [brand name, link]
She offered a 5% prepaid discount. CAC went from Rs 880 to Rs 700 in 10 weeks, measured after returns, down 20%.
[Approved quote, 25-40 words.]
Our takeaway: Sneha measured CAC after returns, which is the stricter test, so her 20% is the most conservative figure here.

WHERE TO START, BY SITUATION
If your product is something people hesitate to try, start with Rohan's sampling sachet. If a large share of your orders is cash on delivery, start with Sneha's prepaid discount and measure after returns. If you already have a phone and a loyal customer or two, start with Aditi's unboxing videos. If your ad account is a maze of audiences, start with Karan's three broad ones.

PRACTICAL TAKEAWAYS
1. Change one thing at a time and measure CAC the same way before and after, for at least six weeks. The windows in this roundup ran from six weeks to four months.
2. Take returned and refused COD orders out of your new-customer count. Otherwise CAC looks lower than it is.
3. Test an offer before a discount: a Rs 49 sachet or a free gift on the first order.
4. Try three broad audiences against your current set-up for about 8 weeks, as Karan did.
5. Add WhatsApp cart recovery within 30 minutes as a separate change, not instead of the above.
6. Write down your CAC today. Without a before figure, none of this is a result.

HOW WE DID THIS
We interviewed the seven founders between 14 and 25 September 2026 and sent each their quote for approval. CAC figures are as each founder reported them and have not been audited. Definitions may differ slightly [define CAC as used in the interviews: confirm]. Aditi Sharma and Rohan Iyer are clients of [Agency name].

GST registration for Etsy and Amazon sellers in Rajasthan: 8 questions answered

If you sell handmade goods from home in Rajasthan on Amazon or Etsy, you have probably heard three different things about GST. This page answers the eight questions craft sellers keep asking us, rule first and detail after. It is written for sellers doing Rs 5-40 lakh a year. The short version: sell through Amazon beyond Rajasthan and you need a GST number [verify]; Etsy export sellers have more choice.

Do I need a GST number (GSTIN) to sell on Amazon from my home in Rajasthan?

Yes, in nearly every case. A seller who supplies goods through an e-commerce marketplace must register for GST whatever the turnover, because the marketplace collects tax at source on the sales [verify].

The one narrow exception is for a seller below Rs 40 lakh who sells only to customers inside Rajasthan; it comes with conditions [verify Notification 34/2023-CT and its conditions]. The moment one order ships to another state, the exception is gone. Most Amazon sellers ship across India, so for most of them registration is the rule, not a choice.

I sell on Etsy to buyers abroad. Do I need GST registration?

Not automatically. For goods in Rajasthan, registration becomes compulsory once your yearly turnover, including export sales, crosses Rs 40 lakh [verify].

Below that, it is your choice, but registering has a practical use. Exports of goods are zero-rated: you can export under a Letter of Undertaking (LUT) without paying IGST, or pay IGST and claim it back [verify]. Both routes need a GSTIN. Keep the bank or payment-gateway proof of foreign currency for every order. If you sell on both Amazon and Etsy, the Amazon rule above decides: you need the number.

Is there a special exemption for handicraft sellers?

Possibly, but do not rely on it yet. A notification exempts some handicraft suppliers from registration below a lower turnover limit, only for goods on a notified list and with conditions [verify the notification number, the goods list and the limit].

Check three things before you lean on it: that your product's HSN code is on the list, that your turnover is below the limit, and that the exemption covers sales through a marketplace [verify]. We check this in the consult.

Can I register at my ghar ka address?

Yes. A home can be your place of business for GST. You upload proof of the address, usually the latest electricity bill, and a consent letter from the owner if the house is in a family member's name [verify the document list on the portal].

Your registration will show the address on every invoice. If you later move your workshop, you must amend the registration; do not keep an old address on the portal.

How long does it take to get the GST number, and what do I need?

About a week in most cases. You need your PAN, Aadhaar, a photo, bank account proof and address proof. When Aadhaar authentication is done, approval is due in 7 working days; otherwise it can take up to 30 days [verify Rule 9 and the current process].

You apply on the GST portal and receive an application reference number (ARN) to track it. If the officer has a question, you get a notice in Form REG-03 and have 7 working days to reply in Form REG-04. Reply on time, with documents; if you miss the date the application can be rejected [verify].

Can I take the composition scheme and pay a flat 1%?

Not if you ship to other states. A composition seller cannot make inter-state sales [verify Section 10]. Since 1 October 2023 a composition seller may sell through a marketplace, but only within the same state [verify].

That rules out the scheme for almost every Amazon seller and every export seller. If you sell only inside Rajasthan, ask us before you choose it; you also lose the right to claim credit for GST on your inputs.

What is TCS, and where does the money go?

TCS is tax collected at source: the marketplace deducts a small percentage of your sales value, currently 0.5% [verify the rate], before it pays you. It is not an extra tax. It shows in your electronic cash ledger and you set it off against the GST you owe [verify].

Illustration, not a client case: you sell Rs 6,00,000 in a quarter. The marketplace deducts 0.5%, which is Rs 3,000. GST on those sales at 5% (the rate depends on your product's HSN code) is Rs 30,000. After the TCS credit you pay Rs 27,000, less any input credit on your materials.

How often do I file returns if I sell very little? (return kab bharna hai)

Every month, or every quarter if you opt for the QRMP scheme, which is open to sellers with turnover up to Rs 5 crore [verify]. You must file even for a month or quarter with no sales.

With the quarterly scheme you file returns every quarter but still pay tax every month. Late filing means a fee per day and interest on tax paid late [verify the fee]. The marketplace also reports your sales to the department, so your return must match its figures. If it does not, you can get a notice.

FROM OUR FILES

[Client case, anonymised: a [craft] seller in [town], Rajasthan, selling on Amazon and Etsy, turnover Rs [x] lakh a year. She came to us because [Amazon asked for a GSTIN before releasing Rs [x] of payouts]. We registered her at her home address in [n] working days, set up an LUT for her Etsy orders, and moved her to quarterly returns. Result: [payouts released; first return filed on time].]

NEXT STEP

Not sure which of these applies to you? Book a Rs 999 registration consult with [Firm name]. We check your products, your marketplaces and your turnover, and tell you what to register for, in one call. [Booking link]

samples.text:
"The first order was for learning, not earning": KaarigarKart's founder on winning US boutiques

Sanjana Chaudhary runs KaarigarKart, a Jaipur marketplace that sells handicrafts to export buyers. In March 2024 a boutique owner in Portland, Oregon found its block-print tablecloths on Instagram and ordered 40 pieces. That one order taught Sanjana what a first export sale really costs: in freight, in paperwork and in margin. For Indian SME exporters eyeing US boutiques, these are useful numbers from someone who paid for them herself, and who is willing to share the bad ones. We asked her what she would tell an exporter before the first quote goes out. This interview has been edited for length and clarity. Sanjana reviewed it for factual accuracy.

**Where did the Portland buyer find you?**
On Instagram. A boutique owner in Portland, Oregon found our block-print tablecloths there.

**And what did she order?**
In March 2024 she ordered 40 pieces, worth Rs 92,000. Before she ordered, she paid for a sample.

**That works out to Rs 2,300 a tablecloth. Did you also go looking for buyers?**
Yes. I sent about 300 Instagram DMs to boutique owners. Fourteen replied. Three of them became orders.

**Fourteen replies from 300 messages is under 5%. Was that discouraging?**
It is what it was: 300 messages, 14 replies, 3 orders. I count it as three orders I would not have had without sending the 300.

**You have said the first order was for learning, not earning. What did you mean?**
Pehla order kamaane ka nahi, seekhne ka tha (the first order was for learning, not earning). It taught me two things. One was about prices, and the other was about the paperwork on the invoice.

**What went wrong with the prices?**
I quoted FOB prices, which means the buyer pays for shipping. The buyer wanted delivered prices, with shipping included. So I absorbed Rs 62,000 of freight.

EXPLAINER: FOB and delivered prices. "FOB" stands for free on board: the seller's price covers getting the goods onto the ship, and the buyer pays the freight from there. Strictly, FOB is a term for sea freight; for air shipments the term is usually FCA. A delivered price includes the shipping, so the seller carries any freight surprise.

**What do you quote now?**
Delivered prices, with shipping included, every time. And every invoice now carries the HS code 6302. I do not send a quote or an invoice without both.

EXPLAINER: the HS code. The Harmonized System is the international way of classifying goods for customs. Heading 6302 covers bed, table, toilet and kitchen linen, which includes tablecloths. Putting the code on the invoice lets customs and the buyer's broker see the same classification [confirm the tariff line for block-print cotton tablecloths with a customs broker].

**Which number should every exporter know before quoting?**
The cost of getting the goods to the buyer. I absorbed Rs 62,000 of freight because the quote did not include it. Today the freight sits inside the delivered price, where the buyer can see it and I can plan for it.

**Any advice for an exporter about to send a first sample?**
Send a paid sample before the first order. That is how the Portland order happened: she paid for a sample first, and then she ordered 40 pieces. I tell every exporter the same thing.

**Let us be blunt: an 18% commission, 14% on courier and customs paperwork, and 11% left on that first order. Was it worth doing?**
Not for the money, no. The marketplace commission is 18%. Courier and customs paperwork took another 14%. My margin on that first order was 11%. On repeat orders my margin is 24%. That gap is why my goal is repeat buyers, not one-off orders.

**So what does success look like?**
Ten boutiques reordering twice a year. That is 20 repeat orders a year from buyers who already know us, at the 24% margin instead of 11%.

**You now name the block-printer on every product page. Why?**
Every product page now names the block-printer who made the piece. Kaarigar ka naam sabse bada brand hai (the artisan's name is the biggest brand).

KEY NUMBERS FROM THE INTERVIEW
First order (March 2024): 40 tablecloths, Rs 92,000, about Rs 2,300 each. Outreach: 300 DMs, 14 replies (under 5%), 3 orders (about one in five of the replies). Freight absorbed: Rs 62,000. Margin: 11% on the first order, 24% on repeat orders.

Jaipur corporation seals 14 of 52 old-city rooftop restaurants over fire safety

JAIPUR, 9 October: The Jaipur municipal corporation sealed 14 rooftop restaurants in the old city on Thursday after inspecting 52 of them in a fire-safety drive that ran from Monday to Wednesday.

The inspected restaurants are in Johari Bazaar, Tripolia Bazaar, Chandpole and Ramganj, according to the corporation. The 14 that were sealed make up more than a quarter of those checked.

Nine of the 14 had no valid fire no-objection certificate (NOC), the corporation said. Six had a single exit blocked by storage. Four used more than the permitted two commercial LPG cylinders. The three counts add up to 19, so some restaurants broke more than one rule.

Lack of a valid NOC was the most common violation among the sealed restaurants: nine of 14, or about two in three.

"A rooftop with one staircase and cylinders next to the exit is a risk to a hundred people on a Saturday night," said Anil Sharma, the corporation's chief fire officer. "We are not closing business for the sake of it."

The other 38 restaurants were given 15 days to comply, according to the corporation [verify: the date the 15 days start from].

The Jaipur Old City Rooftop Restaurants Association said owners had not been told the deadline. "Nobody told us the deadline," said its president, Vikram Shekhawat. "Fourteen families lose Diwali-season income. We are ready to fix everything and ask for seven days." [verify: the corporation's reply to this claim and to the seven-day request]

Owners of sealed restaurants can apply to have the seals removed by submitting a fire-safety compliance certificate by Friday 23 October 2026, according to the corporation [verify: whether this is stated in the sealing notice].

The timelines now overlap. The association has asked for seven days. The 38 restaurants that were not sealed have 15 days. Owners of sealed restaurants have until 23 October, two weeks after the date of this report, to apply to reopen. [verify: who issues the fire-safety compliance certificate, and whether the 15 days run in parallel]

The inspections ran from Monday 5 October to Wednesday 7 October. The corporation sealed the 14 restaurants on Thursday 8 October.

Pandit Ramashray Mishra, Patna tabla maestro and teacher of over 200 students, dies at 84

PATNA: Pandit Ramashray Mishra, the Patna tabla maestro and teacher who was a staff accompanist at All India Radio Patna for 36 years, died at his home in Kankarbagh, Patna, on Tuesday 6 October. He was 84.

His son, Anand Mishra, a school teacher, confirmed the death. The cause was an age-related illness, according to the family.

Mishra mattered for two things that are hard to separate: how he played behind a singer, and how many people he taught to play. For 36 years he accompanied singers at All India Radio Patna. In 1989 he founded a school, the Laya Kendra, where he taught over 200 students and charged nothing to children from poor families.

He was born in 1942 in Laheriasarai, Darbhanga, and began training at the age of nine under Pandit Shivnath Jha in the Banaras gharana. In 1966 he joined All India Radio Patna as a staff tabla accompanist and stayed until 2002.

An accompanist's job is to keep time for someone else. Two colleagues described how Mishra went about it. "He never played over the singer. He listened, and then the tabla answered," said Vidushi Sarita Devi, the Hindustani vocalist, who toured 12 cities with him in 1984.

Arvind Kumar, a sarangi player and a former colleague at All India Radio, recalled the way Mishra rehearsed. "He would rehearse the same sixteen beats for an hour until the room breathed with it," Kumar said. Sixteen beats is the count of teental, one of the most widely played tabla cycles [verify].

Mishra opened the Laya Kendra in Patna in 1989 and taught there for [verify: how many years, and whether until his death]. It taught over 200 students [verify: source of the figure], and children from poor families paid no fee. [Verify: whether the Laya Kendra will continue and who will run it.] [Reporting gap: add one former Laya Kendra student, with name and what they do now, before publication.]

His life was not without a public dispute. In 1994 the state music academy withdrew a senior fellowship of Rs 1 lakh that it had announced for him, after he criticised the selection in a letter to a newspaper [verify: which newspaper, and the academy's full name]. The academy said the selection committee lacked a quorum and that the list was under review. Mishra said it was a punishment for the letter [verify: where and when he said this].

In 1997 a new committee reinstated the fellowship. Mishra accepted it and gave the money to the Laya Kendra.

[Reporting gap: add All India Radio Patna's own statement, if one is issued.]

Mishra is survived by his son Anand and his daughter Mala Jha, and by four grandchildren. His wife, Kamla Devi, died in 2015. The cremation is on Wednesday 7 October at Gulbi Ghat, Patna.

Dr Meena Sinha, principal of a Patna music college [verify: name of the college], put his influence in a line. "Half the tabla teachers in Bihar sat on his floor first," she said.

MISHRA'S LIFE IN DATES
1942: Born in Laheriasarai, Darbhanga.
Around 1951 [verify]: Begins training under Pandit Shivnath Jha, Banaras gharana.
1966: Joins All India Radio Patna as staff tabla accompanist.
1984: Tours 12 cities accompanying Vidushi Sarita Devi.
1989: Founds the Laya Kendra, Patna.
1994: State music academy withdraws an announced Rs 1 lakh senior fellowship.
1997: A new committee reinstates it; he gives the money to the Laya Kendra.
2002: Leaves All India Radio Patna.
2015: His wife, Kamla Devi, dies.
2026: Dies on 6 October, aged 84.

[Lead with the researched fact]
Before we read your GST notice, we rebuild your month from your marketplace payout reports [confirm: this is the firm's actual first step].

[Explain why it makes it better]
Because the tax office's figures come from what marketplaces report about your sales. The quickest way to find the difference is to start from the same data. Cancelled orders, returns and settlement dates sit in the payout report, not in the notice, so a reply built only from the notice has to guess.

[Say what the buyer gets]
You get a one-page reconciliation: every rupee of the difference tied to an order, a credit note or a settlement date, ready to attach to your reply on the GST portal. You do not spend a weekend scrolling through thousands of orders. Illustrative: a Rs 85,000 gap, traced to October credit notes for September orders.

[Invite a test]
Send us one notice and one month of payout reports on WhatsApp: [number]. We send back the reconciliation within [Illustrative: 2 working days]. If we cannot trace the gap, you pay nothing for that first look [Illustrative offer: the firm confirms before use].

samples.brief: 150-250 word piece on TOPICS[0] (a Jaipur CA firm that handles GST notices for D2C brands) following the steps of fw:feynman_technique, each step labelled in [brackets]: Map your knowledge; Teach it to a 12-year-old; Review and refine; Test the rewritten version.
samples.text:
[Map your knowledge]
Topic: why D2C brands get GST notices. GSTR-1 is sales reported. GSTR-3B is tax paid. Marketplaces report your sales too. The scrutiny notice is Form ASMT-10, with 30 days to reply.

[Teach it to a 12-year-old]
Your school keeps an attendance register. Your parents keep a diary of the days you went. If they do not match, the principal asks you to explain. The tax office keeps one notebook from what you file, and another from what marketplaces like Amazon file about you. If the totals differ, it sends a notice asking you to explain. It is not saying you cheated.

[Review and refine]
Gaps: who writes the second notebook, how long you have, what "explain" means. Checked against Rule 99: 30 days.
Rewritten: The tax office compares your return with what marketplaces report about your sales. If they differ, it sends a notice, often a scrutiny notice (Form ASMT-10), asking you to explain. You have 30 days to reply on the GST portal. A good reply is a table: each difference, its reason and the document that proves it. Illustration: return Rs 41,20,000, marketplace Rs 42,05,000; the Rs 85,000 gap is cancelled orders. A difference is not always your mistake, but a missed deadline makes it worse.

[Test the rewritten version]
A newcomer asks: Did I do something wrong? How long do I have? What do I send? The rewritten text answers all three, so it is the one to publish.
samples.writer_note: Rule 99 (30 days, ASMT-10) used as certain; the Rs 41,20,000 / Rs 42,05,000 figures are labelled as an illustration.
